ko.executive_summary: SMIC reports foreign clients repatriating PMIC orders from other fabs back to China, potentially reshaping regional capacity allocation. This suggests cost or lead-time advantages are drawing business to Chinese mature-node capacity amid geopolitical supply-chain diversification.
key_facts: SMIC receiving order shifts from foreign clients back to China

implications.text: Chinese mature-node fabs gaining volume share; potential upside to SMIC's BCD process utilization rates.
Repatriation of orders suggests SMIC may be offering more competitive mature-node pricing or faster delivery than alternative regions.
Concentration of PMIC supply back toward China could reduce geographic redundancy for non-China sourcing strategies.

ko.counterpoint: Single-source claim from SMIC; lacks corroborating customer or volume data to quantify magnitude or sustainability of the order shift.
